methods: expressing everything in sin and cos
statement: By writing $t=\\tan\\theta$, express $\\sin2\\theta$ and $\\cos2\\theta$ in terms of $t$. Hence solve the equation $\\sin2\\theta+\\cos2\\theta=1$ for $0\\le\\theta<2\\pi$, giving your answers in terms of $\\pi$.
solution: With $t=\\tan\\theta$, we have $\\sin2\\theta=\\dfrac{2t}{1+t^{2}}$ and $\\cos2\\theta=\\dfrac{1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}$. Substituting into $\\sin2\\theta+\\cos2\\theta=1$: $\\dfrac{2t+1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}=1$, so $2t+1-t^{2}=1+t^{2}$, i.e. $2t^{2}-2t=0$, so $2t(t-1)=0$. Thus $t=0$ or $t=1$. If $\\tan\\theta=0$ then $\\theta=0,\\pi$. If $\\tan\\theta=1$ then $\\theta=\\pi/4,5\\pi/4$. Hence the solutions are $\\theta=0,\\dfrac{\\pi}{4},\\pi,\\dfrac{5\\pi}{4}$.
hints: Substitute and clear the denominator to get a quadratic in t.
Solve tanθ = 0 and tanθ = 1 for θ in [0, 2π).
